source_text.body:
Generate a backend and frontend app from a prompt
The poster asked Replit's agent for a Go backend with React and TypeScript; it instead built a Task Manager app with a database, so they want a clean start.
·
Apr 8, 2026
Done with
RA
Replit Agent
What they did
The poster tried to start a Replit project for a job interview by prompting the Agent to set up a Go backend with a React, TypeScript, and CSS frontend, but the Agent instead generated a Task Manager app and even added a database. They later found the clean-start path themselves: from the homepage, use Import code or design, then Empty, rather than the main create button; after that, they still had to sort out dependency setup like installing Go.
How it went
It solved the immediate problem of getting to an empty IDE project, but the workflow was confusing enough that another commenter said the same path still opened an Agent chat. The poster also said Replit had changed so much that their interview was ultimately moved to another platform.
Worth knowing
The main catch was outdated documentation: the Imports tab instructions no longer matched the product, so they had better luck asking the Agent about dependency setup.
Try it yourself
with
Replit Agent
Copy prompt
Start a brand-new empty project with a [Go] backend and a [React and TypeScript] frontend. Don't add any sample app, database, or template features I haven't asked for. Set up a health-check endpoint and a frontend page that calls it, and show it working. Then stop and wait for my next instruction.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/replit/comments/1sg7lua/how_do_i_get_to_the_ide
